ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Australian DFAT consolidated sanctions list, and Samoa domestic FIU designations; continuous politically exposed person (PEP) monitoring with enhanced due diligence for any PEP or family member/close associate; adverse media and negative news checks; tiered risk classification (Standard, Medium-Risk Enhanced, High-Risk) with enhanced approval for high-risk PEPs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIFA Company Registry Portal (Samoa International Finance Authority / Registrar of International Companies, Apia, SIFA eRegistry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary corporate name must be expressed in Latin script (English or Samoan) and must not conflict with an existing registered or reserved name. A secondary foreign-language name in Chinese characters may be registered concurrently as a 'foreign name' provided that a Roman-alphabet transliteration is submitted; the Latin-script name remains the official name of the International Company. Names must be distinguishable, not contrary to public policy, and not misleading; all non-Latin characters require translocation into Roman script for registry consistency.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name clearances are submitted through an approved International Company Service Provider (ICSP). If SIFA issues a name refusal, the ICSP may file a written administrative appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of refusal, specifying the grounds of distinguishment and submitting a revised reservation declaration. The Registrar must issue a determination within 30 days; if the appeal is denied, further written appeal may be lodged with the Minister for Commerce, Trade and Labour within 21 days of the Registrar's final decision. Name reservations may be extended by applying to SIFA before expiry upon payment of the statutory extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with conditions. The registered office of an International Company must be a physical address in Samoa, typically the office premises of the licensed registered agent; a virtual office may be acceptable only where it is operated by a licensed International Company Service Provider and is capable of accepting service of process and statutory correspondence. For a VPN/Network Security SaaS business, an offshore International Company does not need an operational office in Samoa, but economic substance filings must demonstrate either exemption as a non-resident foreign business or the existence of adequate activities, assets, and expenditures within Samoa if applicable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Probability (estimated risk less than 5% per annum for a non-licensed offshore ICT holding company; however, SIFA retains statutory power to carry out unannounced inspections and AML/CFT supervisory visits, and the risk increases for high-risk sectors involving payment processing, cryptocurrency, or VPN privacy services).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 3 to 10 and Part IV (registered office and corporate administration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; only one issued share is necessary; no escrow deposit or capital verification mandate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Memorandum and Articles of Association submitted to the Registrar of International Companies are hereby adopted and approved. FURTHER RESOLVED: That share subscriptions be and are hereby allotted to the founding subscribers in the numbers indicated in the Register of Members. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office of the Company be established at [Registered Agent Address] in Apia, Samoa, and that the licensed registered agent be retained as the registered office provider. FINALLY RESOLVED: That [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole director and [Secretary Name] as Secretary, each to hold office until replaced by the shareholders. Signed this date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (via licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name, ending with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.', through the licensed registered agent. The Registrar reviews the name for undesirability, conflict, or confusion with any existing registered company. Upon approval, a name reservation certificate is issued and held for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and name-ending declaration
Subscriber identification documents (passport or national ID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the registered agent immediately files a revised name reservation request with an alternative name; the same review SLA applies and no refund is issued for the previously rejected name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent and notary public in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association including share capital provisions, corporate powers, director and secretary roles, and registered office clause. All subscribers execute the document before a notary public, and the notary certifies the execution and subscriber capacity.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certified passport copies of all subscribers
Proof of residential address of each subscriber
Bank or professional reference letter for each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies incomplete execution or an attestation defect, the affected signature pages are re-signed before the notary and the corrected document is re-drafted prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration Filing and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits the executed Memorandum and Articles, the name reservation certificate, notarized subscriber consents, registered office details, and the government filing fee. The Registrar examines completeness and compliance with the International Companies Act 1987 and, if satisfied, issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office form with Samoa address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect notice, the registered agent has 14 days to file written explanations or corrected documents; any amendment to the Memorandum or Articles is effected by supplemental filing without a second incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and records the registered agent and registered office address. The registered agent confirms acceptance, and the first director and secretary are recorded with their consent forms.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains clerical errors in the corporate name, date, or officer details, the registered agent submits a formal rectification request with the original certificate and a supporting board resolution; correction is processed within the same one-day SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board and licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the first board resolution, approve the issue of share certificates, establish the statutory registers, and appoint banking signatories. The registered agent updates the corporate records and files all required post-incorporation notifications with the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Share certificates and register of members
Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar requests additional corporate governance details, the board adopts a supplemental resolution or amends the registers within 7 days; the registered agent coordinates the submission and all cure costs are borne by the Company.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the entity operates as a remote digital network security and VPN SaaS provider with no physical industrial establishment in Samoa.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – no manufacturing, telecom infrastructure, or physical operational permit is required under Samoan law for this business scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical project, construction, or discharge activities; cloud-based software service only.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no wastewater, VOC, or waste handling thresholds arise from the VPN/privacy application business. If a physical office is later established, general municipal waste disposal and fire safety codes will apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for remote digital operations. If a physical office is leased in Samoa, the Company must obtain a fire safety clearance from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority and an occupational health clearance from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour prior to occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MFRE), Samoa — official e-services portal: https://www.tax.gov.ws/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) must file TIN Application Form (Form TO-01) with the Ministry for Revenue, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of International Companies, the registered-office certificate executed by a licensed Samoan registered agent, director and shareholder particulars, and a certified copy of the company constitution. MFRE processes the application within 5-10 business days and issues a TIN on a non-taxable basis because the IC is exempt from income tax; the TIN additionally enables any VAGST registration, employer registration, or customs transactor code if local transactions arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — A Samoa International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt from all forms of Samoan income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty under sections 199-200 of the International Companies Act 1987, provided no business is conducted within Samoa; the IC discharges its fiscal obligations solely through an annual government fee payable to the Registrar of International Companies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist under Samoan law. The IC must file a statutory declaration under section 201 of the International Companies Act 1987 confirming that it has not carried on business in Samoa and holds no Samoan-situs real property, thereby preserving the tax-exempt classification. The IC cannot elect to be taxed as an ordinary Samoan company; the exempt status is mandatory while the IC remains licensed under the International Companies Act 1987.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 60,000 per annum (approximately USD 22,000) of taxable supplies. An IC deriving wholly offshore VPN/SaaS revenue from non-resident customers has no Samoan place-of-supply nexus and is not registrable for VAGST; where the IC purchases local registered-agent, legal, or audit services, the import of such services may attract VAGST reverse-charge accounting under the VAGST Act 2008.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous-transaction-control mandate exists in Samoa. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue paper or PDF tax invoices containing the particulars prescribed by the VAGST Act 2008 and file periodic returns electronically through the MFRE e-Tax portal; there is no API-based e-invoicing clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of digital VPN, network-security, and privacy-application services is zero-rated under section 8 of the VAGST Act 2008 when the recipient is a non-resident and the services are performed for and effectively enjoyed entirely outside Samoa. The supplier must hold a written contract specifying offshore delivery, non-resident customer identity, and settlement in foreign currency; MFRE may deny zero-rating where evidence demonstrates consumption of the service within Samoa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (required only for physical goods; purely digital services are substantiated by service contracts)
Bill of Lading or service delivery record (e.g., cloud-server deployment log, bandwidth handover report)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Tax Administration Act 2014, a false or fraudulent zero-rating claim attracts a misstatement penalty of up to 75% of the VAGST understated, late-payment interest accruing at 1% per month, and retrospective clawback for up to 4 years. Intentionally false declarations constitute a criminal offense punishable by a fine of up to WST 5,000 and/or two years' imprisonment. Additionally, the Exchange Control Act 1976 empowers the Central Bank of Samoa to impose penalties on non-repatriation of export proceeds beyond the 180-day deadline, notwithstanding the IC's general exchange-control exemption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, Apia; foreign-exchange control is administered by the CBS Exchange Control Department on delegated authority of the Minister of Finance, pursuant to the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1981.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is partially convertible. Samoa accepted IMF Article VIII obligations on 23 June 1994; therefore bona fide current-account transactions (trade in goods, digital services exports, profit and dividend remittances) are free of exchange-control approval barriers, while capital-account transactions (non-resident borrowings, shareholder loans, portfolio investment) remain subject to CBS permission. A Samoa International Company (WS_IC) is treated as a non-resident offshore entity for exchange-control purposes and may hold USD-denominated offshore accounts with licensed commercial banks without conversion to WST. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted and exempt from Samoan withholding tax. Practical hurdles: (i) each material inward and outward remittance requires a bank-presented exchange-control declaration; (ii) banks strictly segregate resident (WST) and non-resident (foreign-currency) accounts to prevent the IC from transacting in the local economy; (iii) correspondent banks apply conservative country-risk scoring, so USD clearing may attract enhanced screening delays of one to three additional banking days.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1981, export proceeds, including proceeds from the export of digital and VPN subscription services, must be fully repatriated and credited to a licensed Samoan bank account within six months of the date of export, and supporting invoices and processor settlement reports must be retained for five years. Mandatory conversion into WST applies only to the portion needed for local-currency expenditure; no surrender requirement applies to foreign-currency accounts designated as non-resident offshore accounts of an International Company. Digital-settlement proceeds received from Paymentwall and similar acquirers in USD may be credited directly to the IC's USD offshore account; the bank must be provided with the processor settlement statement and a narrative describing the underlying subscription service. Failure to substantiate the receipt within the prescribed timeline may cause the bank to reclassify it as export proceeds requiring CBS post-approval filing, with penalties under the Exchange Control Act 1976.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ANZ Bank Samoa Limited (brand transitioning to Bank South Pacific; verify current licence)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium as a primary treasury rail. Leading offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Currenxie, Payoneer) generally exclude Samoa-incorporated companies from their supported-company matrices; Payoneer offers limited settlement support but does not provide a full corporate bank account. Samoa has no domestic EMI licensing regime, and SIFA-licensed international banks operate under a dedicated offshore banking licence with minimum deposit requirements typically above USD 250,000. Structural constraint: Stripe does not list Samoa as an eligible payout country, so a WS_IC cannot directly onboard Stripe with a Samoan bank account; the collection architecture must route subscription card payments through Paymentwall (which can settle to Samoa by SWIFT) or through a separate merchant-of-record in a serviced jurisdiction, a structure that must be separately governed for tax and permanent-establishment risk. Recommended design: licensed Samoan bank USD account as the settlement account; Paymentwall as the acquirer of card and alternative payment methods with MT103 USD payout; EMIs used only for targeted vendor disbursements where they accept Samoan entities. Legal constraints: no Samoa prohibition on using an EMI, but the EMI's licence applies only in its own jurisdiction and cannot be passported to Samoa; all EMI flows must be fully mirrored in the IC's accounting records for Money Laundering Prevention Act compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced profile. Samoan commercial banks will not complete onboarding fully remotely. Standard protocol: (1) pre-screen dossier submitted by the licensed registered agent; (2) bank compliance committee review; (3) in-person interview at the bank's Apia branch, or exceptionally at the registered agent's premises with bank officers attending, where the ultimate beneficial owner presents original passport and proof of address; (4) board resolution authorising account opening and designated signatories; (5) execution of the bank's exchange-control and AML declarations. Video-conferencing may assist document review but does not replace the face-to-face appointment for UBO verification. Expected onboarding timeline: three to six weeks for a clean UBO record; add two to four weeks if the UBO is resident in a non-APG jurisdiction or has prior regulatory flags. Nominee directors do not substitute for UBO identification; banks always look through to the natural person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% non-resident ownership with nominee directors and no local economic footprint in Samoa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed registered-agent attestation; certified passport copies of all natural-person UBOs; UBO declaration filed with the registered agent; complete ownership diagram; source-of-funds statement; bank reference letters from the shareholders' banks; certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing issued by the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: VPN and digital encryption SaaS business classified Medium_Risk_Enhanced (ISIC 6201; NAICS 517919): intangible cross-border revenue, no physical inventory, high transaction velocity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business narrative and product documentation; live website and app-store listings; ISO 27001 or SOC 2 certificate if available; technical network-privacy whitepaper; customer contracts and country revenue split; 12-month Paymentwall and Stripe settlement reports; audited financial statements or accountant's notification; internal AML and transaction-monitoring policy manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Samoa's historic offshore-centre classification causing correspondent-bank de-risking of USD wires.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBS AML/CFT supervision certificate; current FATF/APG mutual-evaluation summary confirming Samoa's compliant status; documentation of removal from the EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions; formal legal opinion from a Samoan barrister confirming the IC's non-resident exchange-control classification; 12 months of bank statements if the entity has banking history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented payment-acquirer routing (Stripe and Paymentwall) suggesting undisclosed third-party settlement or chargeback exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Paymentwall merchant agreement and Stripe service terms; processor chargeback and dispute reports demonstrating chargeback ratio below 1%; end-user refund policy; end-user terms of service; reconciliation ledger mapping processor settlements to the bank account; explanatory note distinguishing acquirer settlement from client-money segregation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from shareholders must be executed as SWIFT MT103 (GPI recommended) in USD from the shareholder's personal or corporate account into the IC's USD capital-escrow or operational account at a licensed Samoan bank. Payment narrative in field 70 must state 'Share subscription - contribution to paid-up capital of WS_IC [entity number]' and must not use payment-for-services codes. The bank will require: (i) a board resolution approving the allotment; (ii) the bank's CBS inward-remittance exchange-control declaration; (iii) source-of-funds evidence for wires above USD 100,000; (iv) post-receipt filing of the allotment return with the registered agent for SIFA records. Shareholder loans are discouraged because they trigger CBS borrowing-permission review; if used, the executed loan agreement, repayment schedule and interest terms must be lodged with the bank in advance. Verification after receipt: the bank issues a transaction advice evidencing the USD balance, which serves as the supporting document for the SIFA share-allotment filing and the annual return.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for all non-documentary settlement: cloud-infrastructure procurement (AWS, Akamai, Microsoft Azure), software licences, contractor fees, registered-agent fees and director salaries; each MT103 must reference the invoice number in field 70 and the corresponding invoice or contract must remain in the treasury file for five years. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are paid by MT103 with narrative 'Dividend distribution of WS_IC', supported by board resolution and solvency confirmation; Samoa levies no withholding tax on International Company dividends and no exchange-control permit is required when paid from the USD offshore account. Documentary commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) are not cost-effective for a SaaS treasury and should be reserved for physical-hardware procurement where a supplier demands one, with the LC issued against the IC's USD account and reimbursements executed by MT103 or MT202. Intra-group disbursements must use MT103 with narrative 'Intra-group payment' and a signed intercompany agreement to prevent re-characterisation as a loan.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards (tenor up to 12 months) with licensed Samoan commercial banks against documented WST/USD commercial exposure; CBS approval embedded in the bank's forward-dealing mandate; speculation prohibited.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) in WST concluded with offshore counterparties where genuine economic exposure is documented; limited onshore liquidity; proceeds received in USD with full hedge documentation retained.
Cross-currency swaps (WST/USD and WST/EUR) with SIFA- or CBS-licensed international banks, subject to prior CBS notification and underlying trade or financial exposure.
Natural hedging through multi-currency accounts maintained in USD, EUR and WST, eliminating unnecessary conversions and reducing reliance on the thin onshore forward market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form AR1) filed by every International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the company's date of incorporation; renewal period runs 1 January to 31 December for license year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of USD 50 per month or part month; continued non-filing after notice may lead to administrative strike-off and restoration fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual License Renewal / Certificate of Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December for the following license year, or within 30 days of anniversary depending on registration cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty assessed per month; persistent default triggers removal from the International Companies Register and loss of legal status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Declaration of Compliance (confirming registered office, directors, and shareholders)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty plus monthly accrual; failure to comply may result in prosecution and strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Samoa Registered Agent (submitted to SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Agent may resign upon non-compliance; company becomes unrepresented and subject to strike-off under International Companies Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: International Companies are exempt from mandatory audit in Samoa unless the company is a licensed bank, insurance, or trustee business; audit is required if shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares request an audited financial statement, or if the company undertakes public offerings / holds a special license under the International Companies Act 1988
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted or permitted by the Samoan International Companies Act; registered agent may require statutory financial records under simplified accounting; Local GAAP applies only for domestic companies, not International Companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa International Companies must maintain a register of beneficial owners at the registered office; annual confirmation must be delivered to the registered agent and SIFA identifying any changes in shareholder, director, or beneficial ownership; share transfers must be approved by directors and recorded in the Register of Members; UBO register updates are due with the annual declaration, and failure to update is an offence subject to penalties

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 1,500 per annum for licensed registered agent, registered office, and compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 for opt-in statutory audit by a Samoan-certified audit firm; not typically required for exempt IC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% standard corporate rate; 0% for tax-exempt International Company (IC)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are fully exempt from income tax on offshore business profits under section 207 of the International Companies Act 1987; no capital gains tax; no stamp duty on offshore transactions; annual government fee is the only impost.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IC-AR (Annual Return of International Company) filed online via Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) corporate registry e-portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of incorporation date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact name and number as per Certificate of Incorporation; no deviation permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa (physical street address, not post office box)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a Samoa-registered registered agent's office; listed agent acts as point of legal service for non-resident owners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, nationality, and number of issued shares of all shareholders and directors
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident individuals, provide passport/ID details and overseas address; bearer shares are prohibited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration confirming no domestic business activity conducted in Samoa and continued compliance with International Companies Act 1987
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declaration must be signed by a director or the registered agent; false declaration is a criminal offence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised capital and paid-up capital (no minimum capital required)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete in WST equivalent; for VPN/SaaS IP licensing company, note that paid-up capital may be immaterial as tax-exempt status is independent of share capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fine of WST 500 plus WST 50 per day; continued default beyond three months triggers automatic strike-off from the International Companies Register under section 172 of the International Companies Act 1987.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IRD-CORP1 (Standard Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via IR Samoa e-Services (reference for standard taxable entities only; ICs are exempt)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end); tax year is the calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to ICs; cited here as the alternative regime if IC tax-exempt status is revoked.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions (expenses directly incurred in income production)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must allocate expenses to Samoa-source income only; overseas overheads excluded.
For a non-resident holding company, zero rate under IC exemption if status upheld.
Calculate only if the company has lost exempt status due to domestic operations or substance failure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 1,000 plus daily surcharge of WST 100; underpayment interest accrues at 2.5% per month; omission or falsification attracts a 150% civil penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by a Samoa International Company to its non-resident shareholders (exempt under IC Act 1987); standard domestic rate is 15% for dividends paid by a taxable resident company to a non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa ICs are tax-exempt and not eligible for treaty relief on dividend outflows as no WHT is imposed. For standard companies, an application for a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) must be made to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue; the recipient must submit the TRC and a completed DTA relief form (IRD-DTA-2) to the payer before distribution, together with a beneficial ownership declaration. Claims are reviewed within 30 business days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for a taxable Samoa company: 15% for royalties and 15% for interest paid to non-residents. For International Companies, payments of royalties and interest to non-residents are statutorily exempt from withholding tax, provided the IC has not engaged in domestic business activities. Relevant DTA provisions (e.g., Samoa-Australia DTA) reduce royalty WHT to 0% and interest WHT to 0% for genuine beneficial owners, subject to CRS/FATCA disclosure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is required for Samoa tax residents (including ICs that have lost exempt status) with related-party transactions exceeding WST 1,000,000 in an income year; Master File is required when aggregate related-party cross-border transactions exceed WST 10,000,000 or where any single related-party royalty/licence exceeds WST 500,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (Samoa ESR 2019) apply to International Companies conducting 'relevant activities', including intellectual property holding, leasing, financing, and distribution/service centres. A VPN network and digital encryption software company is categorised as an IP-rich business; it must demonstrate substantive economic presence in Samoa — i.e., locally situated decision-making management, qualified employees commensurate with activity, sufficient physical office, and adequate expenditure. A shell IC with no employees, no premises, and all decisions taken offshore will fail the substance test, leading to denial of the IC tax exemption and reclassification of its entire income as Samoa-source taxable income at 27%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Misdeclaration of Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a false IC annual return by declaring no domestic business while operating a VPN SaaS platform that provides services to Samoa-resident end users, or misclassifying domestic subscriptions as offshore income to escape 27% standard taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to WST 10,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years under the Tax Administration Act 2015; civil penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall; cancellation of the IC's exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax plus interest; automatic travel ban may be issued by the Commissioner; personal bank accounts frozen; disqualification as corporate director for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Failure of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an IP-licensing and VPN software sales company through a Samoa IC with zero local employees, no controlled premises, and board meetings conducted entirely overseas; using the IC as a passive conduit to avoid taxes in the resident country.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Regulations 2019, failure to satisfy economic substance results in a fine of WST 200,000 plus WST 10,000 per month of continued non-compliance; mandatory filing of missing documentation; the IC's tax exemption is revoked retroactively, exposing all past profits to 27% corporate income tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners personally liable for the tax amount assessed (with limited liability pierced); restrictions on air travel and international transactions; the Supreme Court may issue a 'director disqualification order' under s.62 of the International Companies Act 1987.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting customer payments through Stripe and Paymentwall without performing customer due diligence (KYC), without collecting ultimate beneficial owner identification, and allowing anonymous purchases of VPN network access — creating a money-laundering conduit for encrypted communication payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act (Samoa) 2016, corporate entity is liable to a fine up to WST 2,000,000; the IC's licence or registration may be suspended for up to 12 months; formal warning and remedial order published in the Samoa Gazette.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director and compliance officer are personally exposed to civil penalties of up to WST 250,000 each; criminal liability for 'tipping off' (disclosing a transaction report) carries up to 2 years imprisonment; directors may be stripped of personal assets and a travel ban issued until full restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement / Related-Party Licensing Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting an excessive royalty payment from the Samoa IC to a related overseas IP holder (e.g., a Singapore affiliate) to shift profits out of Samoa, while failing to prepare Local File or to apply the arm's length principle under the Income Tax Act 2015 s.95A.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment re-assessing taxable income at 27%; underpayment interest at 2.5% per month; negligence penalty of 50% of the additional tax; deliberate concealment penalty of 100% of the additional tax; publication of the taxpayer's name in Solomon Star and Samoa Observer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed non-compliant intercompany agreements are personally liable for the underpaid tax amount to the extent of their personal benefit; prohibited from leaving Samoa via 'tax debt travel restraint' order under s.121 of the Tax Administration Act 2015; potential imprisonment for up to 12 months for contempt of a compliance order.
